subject.title: fix: preserve zero sequence ids in sdk events

question: Should the SDK intentionally correct normalized IDs for protocol-valid `seq: 0` events, accepting the narrow compatibility change to previously emitted opaque keys?
rationale: The protocol and dedupe behavior support the fix, but changing a public normalized identifier can affect consumers that persist the old value across upgrades.

options.title: Accept corrected ID semantics
options.body: Land the focused fix after refreshing the branch and confirming required checks, treating the corrected zero-sequence key as the intended SDK contract.

options.title: Preserve existing emitted IDs
options.body: Decline the patch if compatibility with previously generated zero-sequence keys outweighs the protocol-correct dedupe identity.

recommendation.title: Accept corrected ID semantics
recommendation.body: Land the focused fix after refreshing the branch and confirming required checks, treating the corrected zero-sequence key as the intended SDK contract.
